title: Adaptive inflight coalescer to reduce embedding p99 and straggler impact
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: reduce p99 latency for similarity-embedding endpoint (short-to-medium sequences) by addressing straggler requests that inflate micro-batch tail. Approach blends adaptive inflight-cap control with a coalescer that prioritizes short requests and opportunistically drains queues to form efficient kernels. This ticket scopes design, prototype, perf testing, and a staged rollout.

Background: Recent embeds traffic analysis shows bimodal sequence-length distribution and occasional tail events when a long sequence or a small batch gets scheduled into an otherwise efficient micro-batch. Baseline (prod sample, m-embed-v2): p50 22ms, p95 72ms, p99 285ms. Target: p99 <= 140ms while keeping p50/p95 regressions < 10% and maintaining throughput.

Proposed components:
- Inflight cap controller: track per-worker inflight token count and dynamically limit admission for long sequences when short-request backlog is detected.
- Priority coalescer: maintain two logical queues (short / long) and allow the scheduler to form mixed micro-batches with a tunable short-request ratio to bound the impact of long tokens on kernel selection.
- Kernel hinting: propagate sequence-length histogram to kernel selector so it prefers kernels optimized for mixed-length coalesced batches (fused attention code-path suggestion).
- Opportunistic prefetch for KV-cache warmup on predicted hot keys for reranking flows.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict priority could starve long requests; we prefer a soft-slo balancing policy that guarantees a small fraction of throughput for long sequences to avoid starvation.
- Larger coalesced batches improve GPU efficiency but increase tail for individual short requests if admission isn't adaptive. The inflight cap aims to maintain a sweet spot.
- Kernel hinting requires small changes in runtime metadata; we evaluated compatibility costs vs latency gains and elected to keep hints lightweight (histogram + preferred kernel id), avoiding schema churn.

Success metrics (measured on staging & canary):
- p99 <= 140ms (primary)
- p95 <= 90ms
- p50 within 10% of baseline
- No degradation in overall embedding throughput (>95% preserved)
comments: 2026-02-28 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after reviewing Feb embedding dashboard heatmaps; flagged high p99 for reranking workload and provided initial baseline metrics.
2026-03-02 - Marco Nguyen: Ran synthetic load tests on staging with mixed seq lengths. Observed 40% of p99 events come from batches containing a single long sequence mixed into short requests.

2026-03-04 - Evelyn Smith (Perf Eng): Prototype inflight-cap implemented. Initial microbench shows p99 drop from 285ms -> 170ms but p95 increased by ~8% during peak bursts; promising but needs kernel-side tuning.
2026-03-06 - Marco Nguyen: Added priority coalescer that maintains short-first policy with min long-slot per batch. Reduced p99 to ~140ms in 10k req/min test; verified no starvation at steady-state.

2026-03-08 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1129 - Adaptive inflight cap + coalescer prototype. Includes unit tests and runtime flags guarded behind feature flag 'adaptive_coalesce'.
2026-03-09 - UX/Observability: Added temporary chart to perf dashboard - Embed Coalescer: queue depth by length bucket - https://dash.redwood.ai/d/embeddings/embedding-coalescer?orgId=1

2026-03-10 - Marco Nguyen: Kernel hinting added (histogram summary & preferred kernel id). Microbench with fused-attn kernel yields further p99 improvement to ~118ms on A100-40GB. Raised a follow-up to validate multi-GPU compatibility.

2026-03-12 - QA: Running canary against 5% production traffic in us-west-2. Early telemetry: p99 ~125ms, error rate unchanged. Observed slight increase in avg GPU occupancy which aligns with throughput targets.
